primary_activity.atb: ATB (All Terrain Biking) — Gravel, Cyclocross, etc.

motors.operating_modes.e_vehicle_classif.evc/moped: Moped, up to 2 hp and 30 mph

evc/moped.name: Moped, up to 2 hp and 30 mph
evc/moped.description: The moped the classifications naming this group share: a motor of no more than 2 brake horsepower (1,500 W) that can't propel it faster than 30 mph. A vehicle carries this group's id in place of each classification in it.

restrictions.rule: Its motor produces no more than 2 brake horsepower (1,500 W)
The motor can't propel it faster than 30 mph
Past its jurisdiction's e-bike limits; one within them is an electric bicycle instead
Each classification naming this group holds its own jurisdiction's license, registration, insurance, helmet and riding rules

evc/motor_driven_cycle.name: Motor-Driven Cycle, up to 5 hp
evc/motor_driven_cycle.description: The motor-driven cycle the classifications naming this group share: a motorcycle whose motor produces no more than 5 brake horsepower (3,750 W). A vehicle carries this group's id in place of each classification in it.

restrictions.rule: A seat or saddle and no more than three wheels
Its motor produces no more than 5 brake horsepower (3,750 W)
Past its jurisdiction's e-bike limits, and its moped's where the jurisdiction has one
Each classification naming this group holds its own jurisdiction's license, registration, insurance, helmet and riding rules

evc/motorcycle.name: Motorcycle, over 5 hp
evc/motorcycle.description: A road motorcycle whose motor produces more than 5 brake horsepower (3,750 W), which is a motorcycle under every classification naming this group. A vehicle carries this group's id in place of each classification in it.

restrictions.rule: A seat or saddle and no more than three wheels
Its motor produces more than 5 brake horsepower (3,750 W)
Built for highway use; one built for off-highway use is an off-highway motorcycle instead
Each classification naming this group holds its own jurisdiction's license, registration, insurance, helmet and riding rules

evc/off_highway_motorcycle.name: Off-Highway Motorcycle
evc/off_highway_motorcycle.description: An electric motorcycle built for off-highway use, such as an electric dirt bike, ridden under the off-highway category of each classification naming this group. A vehicle carries this group's id in place of each classification in it.

restrictions.rule: Built by its manufacturer for off-highway use, not for the road
No limit on motor power or speed
Kept off public roads except where its jurisdiction allows it
Each classification naming this group holds its own jurisdiction's license, registration, insurance, helmet and riding rules

evc/us/ak/electric_bicycle.name: Electric Bicycle
evc/us/ak/electric_bicycle.description: Alaska's statutes have no electric bicycle category, so on public roads one is a motor-driven cycle. The term is defined only for state parks: a bicycle with fully operable pedals and an electric motor of less than 750 watts, in one of three classes, the first under 500 watts.

restrictions.rule: In state parks, fully operable pedals and an electric motor of less than 750 watts, in three classes: Class 1 pedal assist to 20 mph with a motor under 500 watts, Class 2 throttle to 20 mph, and Class 3 pedal assist to 28 mph
On public roads it isn't a bicycle, which Alaska defines as propelled only by human power, but a motor-driven cycle: the rider needs a driver's license, or at 14 or 15 an M2 permit
The DMV doesn't register e-bikes
In state parks, any class may ride roads open to cars or motorcycles and trails open to off-road vehicles

In state parks, only Class 1 may ride trails open to bicycles, including campground, picnic-area and paved trails, unless a trail is posted closed; a fat-tire Class 1 may ride wherever fat-tire bicycles may
A state park director may temporarily close a trail or area to e-bikes to protect the land, reduce user conflicts or for safety

evc/us/ca/electric_bicycle.name: Electric Bicycle
evc/us/ca/electric_bicycle.description: A bicycle with fully operable pedals and an electric motor that does not exceed 750 watts, in one of three classes: pedal-assist to 20 mph, throttle-capable to 20 mph, or pedal-assist to 28 mph with a speedometer.

restrictions.rule: Fully operable pedals and an electric motor that does not exceed 750 watts
A Class 1 or Class 3 motor can't propel it on its own; Class 1 and Class 2 stop assisting at 20 mph, Class 3 at 28 mph, and a Class 3 must have a speedometer
Not an electric bicycle once modified so the motor alone can exceed 20 mph, the motor exceeds 750 watts, or the pedals are removed
restrictions.citation: California Vehicle Code §312.5, as amended by SB 1271 (2024)

restrictions.rule: Carries a permanent label stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage; it may be modified only if it still meets the definition and its label is replaced to match
No one may sell a product, device or app that changes an electric bicycle's speed so it no longer meets the definition
Must meet the CPSC's bicycle requirements, and its motor must cut out when the brakes are applied or a switch is released
Since January 1, 2026, may only be sold with a battery tested by an accredited laboratory and marked with that laboratory's name or logo
Not a motor vehicle: no driver's license, registration, license plate or insurance

Riders under 18 must wear a bicycle helmet; on a Class 3, every rider and passenger must wear one; a minor's helmet ticket is excused by proof of a helmet and completion of an e-bike safety course, such as the CHP's
Riders must be 16 or older to ride a Class 3, and since January 1, 2026 a Class 3 can't be sold to anyone under 16
Must show a red reflector, or a solid or flashing red light with a built-in reflector, on the rear at all times, not only after dark

Ridden wherever bicycles may go, Class 3 included: since January 1, 2023 no class is barred from bike paths, bikeways or bike lanes, though a local authority may ban any class from an equestrian, hiking or recreational trail it manages, and State Parks from any bicycle path or trail
restrictions.citation: California Vehicle Code §21207.5, as amended by AB 1909 (2022)

restrictions.rule: No city or county may require it to be licensed
A 10 mph prima facie speed limit on sidewalks, and a local authority may set a 10, 15 or 20 mph limit on a bike path or multiuse trail
restrictions.citation: California Vehicle Code §§21214.8, 22352.1, added by AB 2346 (2026)

restrictions.rule: Anything with a motor over 750 watts, that can exceed 20 mph on the motor alone or get assistance past 28 mph, that its maker intends to be modifiable to, or that lacks operable pedals isn't an electric bicycle and can't be sold, advertised or labeled as one; an electric bicycle's label must also name the brand and the manufacturer, importer or distributor
restrictions.citation: California Vehicle Code §§312.5, 28190, as amended and added by SB 1167 (2026)

restrictions.rule: Every new Class 2 must have a speedometer, and every new electric bicycle front and rear lamps
restrictions.citation: California Vehicle Code §28172, added by AB 2346 (2026)

restrictions.rule: Cities in San Mateo County may bar riders under 12 from Class 1 and Class 2 electric bicycles
restrictions.citation: California Vehicle Code §21214.9, added by AB 2595 (2026)

evc/us/ca/moped.name: Moped
evc/us/ca/moped.description: A moped or motorized bicycle: two or three wheels, a motor under 4 gross brake horsepower (3,000 W), and a top speed of 30 mph on level ground.

restrictions.rule: Two or three wheels and an automatic transmission; pedals are optional
Two or three wheels; pedals are optional
restrictions.citation: California Vehicle Code §406, as amended by SB 1167 (2026)

restrictions.rule: Its motor produces less than 4 gross brake horsepower (3,000 W)
restrictions.citation: California Vehicle Code §406, as amended by SB 1167 (2026)

restrictions.rule: Can't propel it faster than 30 mph on level ground
Built for highway use: meets federal motor vehicle safety standards, with a 17-digit VIN and a safety certification label
restrictions.citation: California Vehicle Code §406, as amended by SB 1167 (2026)

restrictions.rule: Riders need a driver's license with an M1 or M2 motorcycle endorsement, so must be 16 or older
Riders must wear a motorcycle helmet
Registered with the DMV and carries a moped plate; registering it doesn't require insurance
Barred from any freeway or expressway where Caltrans or the local authority posts a prohibition
Kept off bike paths and trails unless they run beside a roadway or a local ordinance allows it
A vehicle, not property: it can be towed or impounded

evc/us/ca/motor_driven_cycle.name: Motor-Driven Cycle
evc/us/ca/motor_driven_cycle.description: A light electric motorcycle: its motor produces 5 gross brake horsepower (3,750 W) or less, the electric counterpart of a motorcycle under 150 cc.

restrictions.rule: A motorcycle: a seat or saddle, and no more than three wheels on the ground
Its motor produces 5 gross brake horsepower (3,750 W) or less; one under 3,000 W is a motor-driven cycle rather than a moped when it can go faster than 30 mph
restrictions.citation: California Vehicle Code §405, as amended by SB 1167 (2026)

restrictions.rule: The line is drawn only by an engine under 150 cc, which an electric motor doesn't have
Built for highway use: meets federal motor vehicle safety standards, with a 17-digit VIN and a safety certification label
restrictions.citation: California Vehicle Code §405, as amended by SB 1167 (2026)

restrictions.rule: Riders need a driver's license with an M1 motorcycle endorsement
Riders must wear a motorcycle helmet
Registered and plated with the DMV, and must carry liability insurance
Barred from any freeway or expressway where Caltrans or the local authority posts a prohibition
Kept out of bike lanes except to park, enter or leave the road, or prepare to turn, and off any trail or bike path posted against unauthorized motor vehicles
A vehicle, not property: it can be towed or impounded

evc/us/ca/motorcycle.name: Motorcycle
evc/us/ca/motorcycle.description: A road-registered electric motorcycle: its motor produces more than 5 gross brake horsepower (3,750 W), above what a motor-driven cycle may.

restrictions.rule: A seat or saddle, and no more than three wheels on the ground
Its motor produces more than 5 gross brake horsepower (3,750 W)
One designed primarily for off-highway use, with two wheels, a straddle seat and no pedals, is an off-highway electric motorcycle instead
Riders need a driver's license with an M1 motorcycle endorsement
Riders must wear a motorcycle helmet
Registered and plated with the DMV, and must carry liability insurance
Allowed on freeways
Kept out of bike lanes except to park, enter or leave the road, or prepare to turn, and off any trail or bike path posted against unauthorized motor vehicles
A vehicle, not property: it can be towed or impounded

evc/us/ca/off_highway_electric_motorcycl.name: Off-Highway Electric Motorcycle
evc/us/ca/off_highway_electric_motorcycl.description: An electric motorcycle only permitted in designated OHV areas or on private property; never on streets, sidewalks, bike lanes, bike paths or highways. Can't be registered or converted for street use. No limit on power or speed.

restrictions.rule: Designed by the manufacturer primarily for off-highway use, with two wheels, handlebars, a straddle seat and no pedals from the manufacturer
restrictions.citation: California Vehicle Code §436.1, added by SB 586 (2025)

restrictions.rule: No limit on motor power or speed
Not an electric bicycle or moped, whatever its power, and can't be sold or labeled as an electric bicycle; adding pedals doesn't make it one
Identified with a California OHV Green Sticker from the DMV to ride on public lands, or on private land open to the public
Ridden only in designated OHV areas or on private property; never on highways, streets, sidewalks, bike lanes or bike paths
Can't be registered or converted for street use
No driver's license needed off the highway; riding it on a highway is unregistered, unlicensed operation

evc/us/ca/off_highway_motor_vehicle.name: Off-Highway Motor Vehicle
evc/us/ca/off_highway_motor_vehicle.description: A motor vehicle used only off the highway and not registered for it, such as an electric ATV or off-road quad.

restrictions.rule: Not registered for highway use, so it can't be ridden on a highway, street, sidewalk, bike lane or bike path
Ridden only in designated OHV areas, on public lands open to off-highway vehicles, or on private property
Identified with a California OHV Green Sticker from the DMV to ride on public lands, or on private land open to the public; not needed on private land the owner controls

One that is an all-terrain vehicle (a single seat the operator straddles, three or more low-pressure tires, 50 inches or narrower and 900 lb or lighter) also needs: a motorcycle helmet on everyone aboard, a safety certificate, training course or certified adult's supervision for a rider under 18, a parent or authorized adult supervising a rider under 14, and no passenger unless it's built for one

evc/us/class_1.name: Class 1
evc/us/class_1.description: A pedal-assist electric bicycle: the motor helps only while the rider pedals, and stops helping at 20 mph. Every class is also a federal low-speed electric bicycle (evc/us/low_speed_electric_bicycle).

restrictions.rule: Fully operable pedals, a saddle or seat, and a motor of less than 750 watts
No throttle: the motor assists only while the rider is pedaling
The motor stops assisting at 20 mph, and disengages when the rider stops pedaling or applies the brakes
Carries a permanent label stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage
Must not be modified to change its motor-powered speed or engagement unless the label is replaced to match
Meets the CPSC's bicycle requirements
Ridden wherever bicycles are allowed, including streets, bike lanes and bicycle or multi-use paths
A local authority may ban it from a bicycle or multi-use path only after notice and a public hearing, for safety or legal reasons
On a natural-surface trail designated nonmotorized, the agency that manages the trail decides whether it's allowed
Treated as a bicycle, not a motor vehicle: no driver's license, registration or insurance

evc/us/class_2.name: Class 2
evc/us/class_2.description: A throttle electric bicycle: the motor can propel it without pedaling, and stops helping at 20 mph, by throttle or by pedal assist. Every class is also a federal low-speed electric bicycle (evc/us/low_speed_electric_bicycle).

restrictions.rule: Fully operable pedals, a saddle or seat, and a motor of less than 750 watts
The motor may propel it on its own, with a throttle, but can't assist at all at 20 mph or faster
The motor disengages when the brakes are applied
Carries a permanent label stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage
Must not be modified to change its motor-powered speed or engagement unless the label is replaced to match
Meets the CPSC's bicycle requirements
Ridden wherever bicycles are allowed, including streets, bike lanes and bicycle or multi-use paths
A local authority may ban it from a bicycle or multi-use path only after notice and a public hearing, for safety or legal reasons
On a natural-surface trail designated nonmotorized, the agency that manages the trail decides whether it's allowed
Treated as a bicycle, not a motor vehicle: no driver's license, registration or insurance

evc/us/class_3.name: Class 3
evc/us/class_3.description: A speed pedal-assist electric bicycle: the motor helps only while the rider pedals, and stops helping at 28 mph. Every class is also a federal low-speed electric bicycle (evc/us/low_speed_electric_bicycle).

restrictions.rule: Fully operable pedals, a saddle or seat, and a motor of less than 750 watts
No throttle: the motor assists only while the rider is pedaling
The motor stops assisting at 28 mph, and disengages when the rider stops pedaling or applies the brakes
Must have a speedometer showing its speed in miles per hour
Riders must be 16 or older; a younger passenger may ride on one designed to carry passengers
Riders and passengers must wear a bicycle helmet meeting CPSC or ASTM standards
Carries a permanent label stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage
Must not be modified to change its motor-powered speed or engagement unless the label is replaced to match
Meets the CPSC's bicycle requirements
A local authority may ban it from any bicycle or multi-use path, with no hearing needed
On a natural-surface trail designated nonmotorized, the agency that manages the trail decides whether it's allowed
Treated as a bicycle, not a motor vehicle: no driver's license, registration or insurance

evc/us/co/electric_bicycle.name: Electrical Assisted Bicycle
evc/us/co/electric_bicycle.description: A vehicle with two or three wheels, fully operable pedals and an electric motor of no more than 750 watts, in one of three classes: Class 1 pedal assist to 20 mph, Class 2 throttle to 20 mph, and Class 3 pedal assist to 28 mph.

restrictions.rule: Class 1 and Class 3 assist only while the rider pedals, cutting out at 20 and 28 mph; Class 2 may assist without pedaling, to 20 mph
Class 1 and 3 need a cutoff that can't be bypassed, stopping the motor when the rider stops pedaling; a Class 2 motor stops when the brakes are applied
A vehicle modified out of every class, or built to be easily switched out of one by a button, setting or app, is not an electrical assisted bicycle
restrictions.citation: Colorado Revised Statutes §42-1-102(28.5), as amended by HB 25-1197

restrictions.rule: A multiple-mode e-bike that can switch between classes must meet the rules of each class it can run as
restrictions.citation: Colorado Revised Statutes §42-4-221, as amended by HB 25-1197

restrictions.rule: A multiple-mode e-bike's label must name each class it can run as
restrictions.citation: Colorado Revised Statutes §42-4-221, as amended by HB 25-1197

restrictions.rule: Carries a permanent label, in Arial at least 9-point, stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage, and must not be modified to change its speed or motor engagement unless the label is replaced to match
Sellers must disclose its wattage, top speed and class; selling a vehicle that isn't one as an e-bike without a written disclosure is a deceptive trade practice
restrictions.citation: Colorado Revised Statutes §42-4-221, as amended by HB 25-1197

restrictions.rule: Its lithium-ion battery must be certified by an accredited lab to a UL 2849 or EN 15194 battery standard
restrictions.citation: Colorado Revised Statutes §42-4-221, as amended by HB 25-1197

restrictions.rule: Meets the CPSC's bicycle requirements (16 CFR part 1512)
Class 3 riders must be 16 or older; a younger passenger may ride on one designed to carry passengers
Class 3 riders and passengers under 18 must wear a bicycle helmet meeting CPSC or ASTM standards, and a Class 3 must have a speedometer
Class 1 and Class 2 may ride bike and pedestrian paths where bicycles are allowed, but a local authority may ban them from its paths
Class 3 is kept off bike and pedestrian paths unless the path is within a street or highway or the local authority allows it
On a sidewalk it yields to pedestrians, and local ordinances or signs may ban it there
In state parks, Class 1 and 2 may ride roads, bike lanes and trails open to bicycles; in state wildlife areas, e-bikes are limited to roads and camping or parking areas open to motor vehicles
Its rider has the same rights and duties as a bicyclist, and it is not a motor vehicle: no registration or driver's license

evc/us/in/electric_bicycle.name: Electric Bicycle
evc/us/in/electric_bicycle.description: A bicycle with operable pedals and an electric motor with a power output of no more than 750 watts, in one of three classes: Class 1 and Class 3 pedal-assist up to 20 and 28 mph, and Class 2 throttle-assisted up to 20 mph.

restrictions.rule: A bicycle with operable pedals and a motor with a power output of no more than 750 watts
Class 1 assists only while the rider pedals and stops at 20 mph; Class 2 can be throttle-propelled up to 20 mph; Class 3 assists only while pedaling and stops at 28 mph
The motor must disengage or stop assisting when the rider stops pedaling or applies the brakes
Meets the CPSC's bicycle requirements (16 CFR part 1512)
Carries a permanent label stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage; anyone who modifies its speed or motor engagement must update the label
Class 3 riders must be 15 or older; a younger passenger may ride on one designed to carry passengers
Class 3 riders and passengers under 18 must wear a bicycle helmet meeting CPSC or ASTM standards
Regulated as a bicycle, with a bicycle rider's rights and duties, and may be ridden wherever bicycles may
Class 1 and Class 2 may use bicycle and multipurpose paths open to bicycles unless a statute, rule or local ordinance says otherwise
Class 3 is kept off bicycle and multipurpose paths unless the path runs within or beside a highway or the local authority or state agency in charge allows it
On a natural-surface trail designated nonmotorized, the local authority or state agency that manages it decides which classes are allowed
On DNR properties all classes may use roads, Class 1 and Class 2 may use paved and gravel trails, and only Class 1 may use natural-surface trails open to bicycles
Not a motor vehicle: no driver's license, title, registration or insurance, and exempt from off-road vehicle rules

evc/us/nc/electric_bicycle.name: Electric Assisted Bicycle
evc/us/nc/electric_bicycle.description: A bicycle with two or three wheels, a seat or saddle, fully operable pedals and an electric motor of no more than 750 watts. From December 1, 2026 it falls in one of three classes: class 1 pedal assist and class 2 throttle, both to 20 mph, and class 3 pedal assist to 28 mph; until then its motor alone may not push it past 20 mph.

restrictions.rule: Two or three wheels, a seat or saddle, fully operable pedals and a motor of no more than 750 watts
Its top speed on motor power alone on level ground is 20 mph
Class 1 assists only while the rider is pedaling and class 2 can propel it without pedaling, both to 20 mph; class 3 assists only while pedaling, to 28 mph
restrictions.citation: N.C. Gen. Stat. §20-4.01(7a), as amended by Session Law 2026-46

restrictions.rule: Riders and passengers under 18 on a class 3 must wear a helmet meeting federal safety standards
restrictions.citation: N.C. Gen. Stat. §20-171.3, enacted by Session Law 2026-46

restrictions.rule: No statewide minimum age
Not a motor vehicle: no driver's license, registration or insurance
The rider has the duties of a vehicle driver under the traffic laws

It may be ridden on all roadways, bicycle lanes and multiuse paths, except where a city or county restricts it, or the Department of Natural and Cultural Resources does in state parks and historic sites
restrictions.citation: N.C. Gen. Stat. §20-171.3, enacted by Session Law 2026-46

restrictions.rule: Cities and counties may restrict classes and set speed limits on multiuse paths and sidewalks, and may require helmets for riders and passengers under 18 on class 1 and class 2

One past these limits with pedals that tops out at 20 mph is a motor-driven bicycle, under motorcycle rules; one with no external shifter that tops out at 30 mph is a moped, which needs registration, insurance, a helmet and a rider 16 or older; any other is a motorcycle

evc/us/nj/dirt_bike.name: Dirt Bike
evc/us/nj/dirt_bike.description: A two-wheeled motorcycle designed and manufactured for off-road use only that doesn't meet federal motor vehicle safety standards or EPA on-road emissions standards, such as an off-road e-moto.

restrictions.rule: Two wheels, designed and manufactured for off-road use only, and not compliant with federal motor vehicle safety standards or EPA on-road emissions standards
Registered with the Motor Vehicle Commission to ride on public lands or waters or to cross a public highway
The rider must carry proof of liability insurance and current registration
Riders must be 14 or older on public lands or waters or crossing a public highway
Riders under 18 must complete an approved safety course and carry the certificate while riding
For off-road use only
Banned from all New Jersey state parks and forests

evc/us/nj/electric_bicycle.name: Low-Speed Electric Bicycle
evc/us/nj/electric_bicycle.description: A two-wheeled bicycle with fully operable pedals and an electric motor that helps only while the rider pedals and stops helping at 20 mph.

restrictions.rule: Two wheels and fully operable pedals; the motor assists only while the rider is pedaling and stops assisting at 20 mph
restrictions.citation: N.J.S.A. 39:1-1, as amended by P.L.2025, c.285

restrictions.rule: The definition sets no motor wattage limit

An e-bike with a throttle, or with pedal assist past 20 mph up to 28 mph, is a motorized bicycle instead: it also needs a license and registration, must carry liability insurance, and is barred from roads posted over 50 mph
One with pedals and a motor over 750 watts that can exceed 28 mph is an electric motorized bicycle, which the law counts as a motorcycle
Riders must be 15 or older
Riders need a driver's license or a motorized bicycle (e-bike) license from the Motor Vehicle Commission, which takes a knowledge test and a road test; 15- and 16-year-olds need the e-bike license
Registered with the Motor Vehicle Commission, with its two plate stickers displayed on the front fork; required since July 19, 2026, after a six-month grace period
No insurance required
Riders under 17 must wear a bicycle helmet
Ridden on streets, highways and bicycle paths; a county or municipality may ban it from bicycle paths it controls
May be parked on a sidewalk if it doesn't block pedestrians
Kept off natural-surface trails designated non-motorized unless the local authority allows it
Selling a kit that converts it into a motorized or electric motorized bicycle is prohibited
Not a motor vehicle; the laws that apply to bicycles otherwise apply to it
A bike-share rider 16 or older needs no license, and the rider doesn't register a shared e-bike

evc/us/ny/electric_bicycle.name: Bicycle With Electric Assist
evc/us/ny/electric_bicycle.description: A bicycle no more than 36 inches wide, with operable pedals and an electric motor of less than 750 watts, in one of three classes: class 1 pedal assist and class 2 throttle, both to 20 mph, and class 3, which may run on the motor alone to 25 mph and is allowed only in a city of a million or more people.

restrictions.rule: No more than 36 inches wide, with operable pedals and an electric motor of less than 750 watts
Class 1 assists only while the rider is pedaling and class 2 may be propelled by the motor alone; both stop assisting at 20 mph
Class 3 may be propelled by the motor alone and stops assisting at 25 mph; it may be ridden only in a city of a million or more people, which means New York City
Meets the CPSC's bicycle requirements (16 CFR part 1512)
Carries a label stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage, required since June 1, 2022
Riders must be 16 or older
Class 3 riders must wear a helmet
Not registered with the DMV
State law allows it on roads with a posted speed limit of 30 mph or less and in bicycle lanes
Not ridden on a sidewalk unless a local law allows it; may be parked on one if it leaves pedestrians room to pass
Cities, towns and villages may further regulate when, where and how it's ridden, including speed limits, helmets and reflective gear; New York City has capped e-bikes at 15 mph since October 24, 2025
On public lands other than roads it may be ridden only where the agency in charge authorizes it

State parks allow class 1 and class 2 on boardwalks and paved or improved paths at up to 15 mph, and class 1 alone on natural-surface trails open to bicycles; class 3 is banned at every state park facility, and all classes from parkways
Breaking these rules carries a civil fine of up to $50

evc/us/pa/electric_bicycle.name: Pedalcycle With Electric Assist
evc/us/pa/electric_bicycle.description: A single category, not the three-class system: a pedalcycle of 100 pounds or less with operable pedals and an electric motor rated at no more than 750 watts that can't propel it past 20 mph on its own, legally a bicycle.

restrictions.rule: Weighs no more than 100 pounds, with two or three wheels more than 11 inches in diameter
restrictions.citation: Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes Title 75 §102, as amended by Act 154 of 2014

restrictions.rule: Operable pedals and an electric motor rated at no more than 750 watts
The motor alone can't propel it faster than 20 mph on a level surface; a throttle is allowed
No class system: Pennsylvania has not adopted the three-class model law
Riders must be 16 or older
Riders and passengers under 12 must wear a bicycle helmet, including a child in a bike seat or towed trailer
Carries only as many riders as it's designed for, though an adult may carry a child in an attached child seat or trailer
No driver's license, title, registration or insurance
Follows the same rules of the road as a bicycle; banned from freeways
May be ridden on sidewalks, yielding to pedestrians, except in a business district unless signs allow it or where a bike lane runs alongside

In state parks and forests, allowed on roads and on trails open to bicycles, but must be pedaled, not run on throttle alone, on non-motorized trails; barred from natural areas and yellow- or orange-blazed hiking trails
A parent may not knowingly let their child break these rules; a violation is a summary offense with a $10 fine
One with pedals and an automatic transmission that exceeds these limits but has a top design speed of 25 mph or less is a motorized pedalcycle, a motor vehicle that needs a Class C driver's license

evc/us/tx/electric_bicycle.name: Electric Bicycle
evc/us/tx/electric_bicycle.description: A bicycle with fully operable pedals and an electric motor of fewer than 750 watts, with a top assisted speed of 28 mph or less, in one of three classes: Class 1 pedal assist to 20 mph, Class 2 throttle to 20 mph, and Class 3 pedal assist to 28 mph.

restrictions.rule: Fully operable pedals and an electric motor of fewer than 750 watts, with a top assisted speed of 28 mph or less
Class 1 assists only while the rider pedals, to a top assisted speed of 20 mph
Class 2 can be propelled by its motor without pedaling, to a top assisted speed of 20 mph
Class 3 assists only while the rider pedals, to a top assisted speed of more than 20 but less than 28 mph, and must be sold with a speedometer
May only be ridden if the motor disengages when the rider stops pedaling or applies the brakes
Carries a permanent label stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage; anyone who changes its motor-powered speed or engagement must replace the label to match
Meets the CPSC's bicycle requirements
Class 3 riders must be 15 or older; a younger passenger may ride on one
No statewide helmet requirement
No driver's license, title or insurance, and it can't be registered for highway use
TxDOT and local authorities may not ban it from roads used mainly by motor vehicles, or from anywhere a regular bicycle may go, except natural-surface trails closed to motor vehicles
TxDOT and local authorities may ban bicycles, e-bikes included, from sidewalks and set speed limits on bicycle paths

evc/us/tx/off_highway_motorcycle.name: Off-Highway Motorcycle
evc/us/tx/off_highway_motorcycle.description: A motorcycle ridden for off-highway recreation, one of the off-highway vehicles that need a Texas Parks and Wildlife decal on public riding land, which is how an off-road electric dirt bike is ridden legally.

restrictions.rule: Counted as an off-highway vehicle under the state's off-highway trail program, which sets no limit on motor power or speed

Needs an annual off-highway vehicle decal from Texas Parks and Wildlife, at least $8 and valid September through August, to ride on public land or land developed with a department grant where off-highway riding is legal

The Transportation Code calls a seated two-wheeler with an electric motor that isn't designed for highway use and can't be titled a pocket bike or minimotorbike, and nothing in Texas's scooter law authorizes one on a road, street, bicycle path or sidewalk
The all-terrain vehicle rules, including their safety certificate, cover only vehicles on three or more tires
